name: NIST SP 800-63
full_name: NIST SP 800-63-4 Digital Identity Guidelines (with 800-63A, 800-63B and 800-63C)
issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology
notice: Requirements are the SHALL and SHALL NOT statements of NIST SP 800-63-4 and its three volumes, quoted word for word. Many apply only at a given identity, authentication or federation assurance level, or only to a particular authenticator type or federation model; mark the others not applicable.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-63A-4, Digital Identity Guidelines: Identity Proofing and Enrollment
NIST SP 800-63B-4, Digital Identity Guidelines: Authentication and Authenticator Management
NIST SP 800-63C-4, Digital Identity Guidelines: Federation and Assertions

control_flags.type: section for a numbered section of a volume that contains SHALL requirements.

scoring.summary: Percentage of applicable sections that conform, with partial conformity counting as half. NIST defines no score; this is an HCG measure.

rules.summary: Every SHALL and SHALL NOT statement is mandatory for conformance, so a section conforms only when each of its applicable requirements is met.
rules.quote: indicate requirements to be followed strictly in order to conform to the publication and from which no deviation is permitted.

rules.summary: Requirements tied to an assurance level (IAL, AAL or FAL) apply only when that level is selected for the service, and requirements for a given authenticator type or federation model apply only when it is used; others are marked not applicable.
rules.quote: The output of this step is a set of assigned xALs and baseline controls for each user

rules.summary: A partially conforming section counts as half. This is an HCG convention.

glossary.definition: Identity assurance level: the strength of the identity proofing process.
Authentication assurance level: the strength of the authentication process.
Federation assurance level: the strength of the federation process and assertions.
Credential service provider: the entity that issues or registers subscriber authenticators.
Relying party: the entity that relies on the subscriber's authenticators or a federated assertion to grant access.
The ability of an authentication protocol to prevent the disclosure of authentication secrets and valid authenticator outputs to an impostor verifier.
